subsections.subsection_title: How to report an ultrasound systematically

blocks.text: This is an excellent OSCE mnemonic.

"This is a singleton live intrauterine pregnancy. The gestational age is consistent with the established dates. The fetal anatomy visualised appears normal on this examination, with no obvious structural abnormality identified. Fetal biometry is appropriate for gestational age, with estimated fetal weight around the appropriate centile. The placenta is posterior and clear of the internal cervical os. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. There are no obvious sonographic features of fetal compromise on this examination."

"The estimated fetal weight is below the 10th centile, which raises concern for a small-for-gestational-age fetus and possible fetal growth restriction. I would assess growth trajectory, liquor volume and Doppler studies and arrange appropriate obstetric/fetal medicine follow-up."

blocks.text: "You have a fetus with an estimated weight below the 10th centile. What would you do?"

"I would not automatically label this as pathological growth restriction. I would assess the clinical context and growth trajectory, confirm fetal biometry, assess amniotic fluid and perform appropriate Doppler studies, particularly umbilical artery Doppler. I would then determine whether the fetus is constitutionally small or has evidence of fetal growth restriction and arrange appropriate surveillance."
That answer demonstrates clinical reasoning rather than simply reading numbers.
